summary: Build domain-specific connection profiles for databases, storage backends, and APIs on top of the profiles framework. Define a ProfileDescriptor with typed parameters, register it via a Registry, and get a fully validated settings class with authentication, secret handling, and template derivation built in. You can also extend the auth system with custom authentication modes for any backend.
use_cases: Create a PostgreSQL connection profile that exposes host, port, database, and schema as typed fields with auto-derived connection strings
Add a custom OAuth2 + refresh-token auth mode for a proprietary API and wire it into an existing profile descriptor
Build a cloud storage profile with tiered parameters where advanced options only appear when explicitly configured
Publish a profile registry as a standalone package that downstream teams install and use with their own config files

concepts.name: Defining a profile descriptor
concepts.description: A ProfileDescriptor declares the connection's identity (name, provider_type), its typed parameters via ParameterSpec entries, and which auth modes it supports. Each ParameterSpec defines a name (UPPERCASE by convention), Python type, tier, default value, driver_key mapping, and optional secret/transform/validator/template behaviour. Use the MISSING sentinel for required fields.

concepts.name: Registering and using a profile class
concepts.description: Create a Registry for your domain, then use @REGISTRY.decorator() on a DescriptorProfile subclass that declares __descriptor__. The framework automatically installs typed Pydantic fields from your descriptor at class creation time. Implement __adapter__ to provide a custom output pipeline that transforms profile values into driver-ready kwargs.

concepts.name: Auth mode extension
concepts.description: Create new auth modes by subclassing AuthSpec with a unique kind literal. Register it in AUTH_TO_DRIVER_KWARGS for default dispatch, or override _auth_kwargs() in your DescriptorProfile subclass for full control over how credentials are mapped to driver parameters.

concepts.name: Invariant test coverage
concepts.description: Call descriptor_invariants_for(MY_REGISTRY) and assign the result to a test class to get automatic coverage of descriptor conventions: lowercase names, UPPERCASE parameter names, unique driver_keys, valid auth_modes, and non-null provider_type. This gives you confidence that your descriptors are well-formed as your profile evolves.

concepts.name: Secret fields in profiles
concepts.description: Set secret=True on a ParameterSpec and the framework wraps the field as SecretStr automatically. When building driver kwargs, _default_kwargs() unwraps secrets via .get_secret_value(), so downstream driver code receives plain strings while the settings object keeps credentials masked in logs and repr output.

concepts.name: Template-derived fields in profiles
concepts.description: Set a template string on a ParameterSpec (e.g., '{OTHER_FIELD}/suffix') and post_init() computes the value automatically when the field still holds its declared default. Explicit user-provided values always take priority, so templates serve as smart defaults that adapt to the rest of the configuration.
